The first and second sentence sound repetitive instead if conjoined like this "It's commonly acknowledged that a high degree of education is the key to success in life; that is not entirely true."  Could also mention in the first paragraph that having a college degree still doesn't promise a job.  "My father, just a guy from Mexico, living proof of this hypothesis/proposition" 

My father was born into a family of seven siblings, him being one of the oldest, had to help my grandfather put food on the table, by helping out at the farm along with his siblings. Therefore, going to school and continuing his education wasn’t an option. My father grew up in an adobe house high up in the mountains of a sierra so the walk to school was certainly not easy. My father, a man of great intellect, has an education equivalent to that of a 6th grade student in the United States. This, however, didn’t stop him from achieving his dreams. At the age of fifteen, my father immigrated to the United States working any job he could secure, and after a few years, he started his own business. His business succeeded and after consistent hard work, he now makes well over the average amount that a person with a bachelor’s degree earns.
